purpose: Quantify how often fixed-coordinate site definitions would infer turnover between successive breeding seasons despite continuous source-provided named-colony identity.

input_rule.include: Rows with origin_match=true and parseable date for Astrid, Mertz or SANAE.

annual_anchor.rule: Within each colony-season, select the earliest observation date; if multiple published route-origin points occur on that date, project them to EPSG:3031 and use their arithmetic centroid.
annual_anchor.consecutive_transition: Only adjacent season labels differing by exactly one breeding season enter the primary denominator.

estimands.primary: For each radius r, fraction of consecutive-season named-colony transitions whose annual-anchor displacement exceeds r.
estimands.by_colony: Same false-turnover curve separately for Astrid, Mertz and SANAE.
estimands.identity_preserving_radii: q50, q90 and q95 of consecutive-season anchor displacement.
estimands.long_jump_context: Report maximum transition and its colony/seasons descriptively; do not create a post-hoc threshold.

inference: descriptive; no p-values because only three named colonies are independent biological series
boundaries: False turnover is disagreement between fixed-coordinate node identity and source-provided named-colony identity; it is not proof of identical individual birds.
Do not infer dispersal mechanism or environmental cause.
Do not change radii after viewing displacement.
The independent 2024 SAR source evaluates within-season aliasing and is not pooled into the interannual denominator.
stop_rule: After this curve is computed, do not search additional radii or selectively omit large transitions.
